page.title: Books & Accounts
page.purpose: Show the accounting entities an operator keeps and the accounts inside them, so personal and business money share one system without being mixed.

priorities.statement: Which book each account belongs to, unambiguously
Each account's balance, with the basis and age of the inputs behind it
Movement between books, modelled rather than lost
Account administration, ranked below the three above

states.description: Books and their accounts at rest.
Nothing in flight; the surface is at rest and its controls are usable.
A user-triggered operation is in flight and its outcome is not yet known.
An operation completed; the result is announced, not merely rendered.
First read of the surface's data; layout is reserved so nothing shifts on arrival.
A write is in flight; the affected control is disabled and says why.
A background read is refreshing data the user is already looking at.
A user-requested re-read of data already on screen.
No books or accounts exist yet — first run.
Some contributing source could not be read; what is missing is named.
Displayed data is older than its freshness window; its age is shown.
Input was rejected before submission; the offending field is identified.
The request failed; the reason and the next action are stated.
An automatic retry is in progress; attempt count and next attempt are visible.
The caller's role does not permit this; what role would is stated.
The client cannot reach the API; queued or read-only behavior is explained.
More than one book exists — typically a personal and a business entity. Every account is attributed to exactly one of them.
A movement between two books is present, shown as a linked pair rather than as an unexplained outflow in one book and inflow in the other.
An account's balance is missing a contributing source. The balance is shown with the gap named, never silently completed.

elements.name: Books
elements.description: The accounting entities the operator keeps. Each account belongs to exactly one.
The book an account belongs to, stated on the account itself rather than implied by grouping alone.

elements.name: Accounts
elements.description: Accounts with kind and balance. Balances are compared down the column, so they share a decimal alignment.
The basis and age of the inputs behind a balance, shown beside the figure.
Names the source missing from a balance when it could not be fully computed.
Links the two sides of an inter-book transfer so neither reads as unexplained money appearing or vanishing.
First-run guidance explaining what a book is and why the personal/business split exists before asking for one.

claims.statement: Every account states which book it belongs to, rather than relying on visual grouping alone.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-001. Grouping is lost to a screen reader, to a sorted view, and to a filtered one — and mixing personal and business money is the failure this model exists to prevent.

claims.statement: A movement between books is presented as a linked pair rather than as two unrelated events.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-001 requires inter-book movement to be modelled rather than lost. An unlinked pair reads as income in one book and a loss in the other, which is wrong in both.

claims.statement: A balance that could not be fully computed is shown with the missing source named.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-003 and the honesty rule. A balance is derived at read time; a partial derivation must say so or it is indistinguishable from a complete one.

claims.statement: Each balance is accompanied by the basis and age of the inputs behind it.
claims.rationale: PRD honesty rule. Balances are the figures most likely to be read as fact, so they are the figures that most need their provenance adjacent.

claims.statement: The first-run state explains what a book is before asking the operator to create one.
claims.rationale: 'Book' is domain vocabulary the target user does not have. An empty form labelled with an unfamiliar noun is the most likely abandonment point in the product.

claims.statement: Balances share a decimal alignment and use tabular numerals so magnitudes are comparable down the column.
